story_description: Implement reliable lifecycle management for the Codex CLI app-server daemon including startup, health monitoring, graceful shutdown, and automatic restart capabilities to ensure consistent communication between the Blaze harness and the Codex backend.
task_description: Create a Swift actor responsible for starting, stopping, monitoring, and restarting the Codex CLI app-server process with health checks, timeout handling, and state transitions exposed via async/await APIs.
atom_description: Implement CodexAppServerManager actor in Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerManager.swift providing full lifecycle control for the Codex app-server daemon. The manager handles process spawning via Foundation.Process, port allocation, health check polling via HTTP GET to /health endpoint, graceful SIGTERM shutdown with SIGKILL fallback, automatic restart on crash detection, and state machine transitions (stopped, starting, running, stopping, error). Exposes async methods start(), stop(), restart(), and observable @Published state for UI binding.
problem_statement: The Blaze harness needs to communicate with Codex CLI via its app-server mode for advanced scenarios like persistent sessions and structured event streaming. Without a dedicated lifecycle manager, the app would have to manually spawn processes, track PIDs, handle crashes, and coordinate shutdown - all error-prone operations that belong in a single responsible component. The manager must handle the daemon lifecycle reliably across app launches, backgrounding, and unexpected terminations.

Process spawning using Foundation.Process with stdout/stderr pipe capture
Port allocation finding available port in configured range 9100-9199
Automatic restart on unexpected process termination with configurable max retries
Observable @Published state property for SwiftUI binding
Delegate protocol for lifecycle event callbacks to adapter layer
Configurable timeouts for startup, health check, and shutdown operations

scope_out: Port and auth configuration UI (handled by X005-CONFIG)

assumptions: Codex CLI binary is installed at a known path discoverable via which codex or PATH
App-server mode is invoked via codex app-server --port <port> --json command
Health endpoint responds to HTTP GET /health with 200 OK when ready
App-server process exits cleanly on SIGTERM within 5 second grace period
Port range 9100-9199 is typically available on developer machines
macOS 14+ provides reliable Process termination notifications
App-server stdout emits JSON events for event stream (consumed by X003-EVENTS)
Single app-server instance per Blaze app is sufficient for initial release
constraints: Must use Foundation.Process for subprocess management (no third-party deps)
Must be an actor to ensure thread-safe state management
All public methods must be async for non-blocking operation
Must not block main thread during process spawn or health checks
State transitions must be atomic and validated to prevent race conditions
Must handle app termination gracefully by stopping daemon
Health check interval must be configurable between 1-60 seconds
Startup timeout must be configurable between 5-120 seconds
Must log all state transitions at info level for debugging
Must not store Codex auth tokens (handled by Codex CLI keychain)
functional_requirements: FR-01: start() must spawn Codex app-server process with configured port and JSON output mode
FR-02: start() must poll /health endpoint until 200 response or timeout exceeded
FR-03: start() must transition state from stopped to starting to running on success
FR-04: start() must transition to error state with descriptive error on failure
FR-05: stop() must send SIGTERM to process and wait up to gracePeriod seconds
FR-06: stop() must send SIGKILL if process does not exit within grace period
FR-07: stop() must transition state from running to stopping to stopped
FR-08: restart() must call stop() then start() with exponential backoff on repeated failures
FR-09: healthCheck() must return HealthStatus with latency, version, and uptime info
FR-10: Manager must detect unexpected process termination and attempt auto-restart
FR-11: Manager must respect maxRestartAttempts limit to prevent restart loops
FR-12: Manager must find available port by checking socket availability in range
FR-13: Manager must capture process stdout/stderr for logging and event parsing
FR-14: Manager must notify delegate of state changes for adapter coordination
FR-15: Manager must clean up zombie processes on app termination via atexit handler
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: State transitions must complete within 100ms excluding I/O waits
NFR-02: Health check round-trip must complete within 1 second timeout
NFR-03: Memory footprint of manager must not exceed 1MB including buffers
NFR-04: Must handle 1000 rapid start/stop cycles without resource leaks
NFR-05: All async operations must be cancellable via Task cancellation
NFR-06: Logs must use OSLog with appropriate log levels (debug, info, error)
implementation_steps: Create Blaze/Sources/Engine/ directory if not exists
Create CodexAppServerManager.swift with file header and imports (Foundation, OSLog, Combine)
Define AppServerState enum with cases: stopped, starting, running, stopping, error(AppServerError)
Define AppServerError enum with cases: binaryNotFound, portUnavailable, startupTimeout, healthCheckFailed, unexpectedTermination
Define HealthStatus struct with isHealthy (Bool), latency (TimeInterval), version (String?), uptime (TimeInterval?)
Define AppServerManagerDelegate protocol with methods: didChangeState, didReceiveOutput, didTerminateUnexpectedly
Define CodexAppServerManager actor with private properties: process (Process?), port (Int), state (AppServerState), restartAttempts (Int)
Add @Published state property using CurrentValueSubject for Combine observation
Implement private findAvailablePort() -> Int? checking socket availability in range 9100-9199
Implement private spawnProcess(port: Int) throws -> Process creating Process with codex app-server arguments
Implement private waitForHealthy(timeout: TimeInterval) async throws polling /health until success
Implement public start() async throws orchestrating spawn, health wait, and state transitions
Implement public stop() async sending SIGTERM, waiting grace period, then SIGKILL fallback
Implement public restart() async throws with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s) on failures
Implement public healthCheck() async throws -> HealthStatus making HTTP request to /health
Implement private handleProcessTermination() detecting unexpected exit and triggering restart
Set up Process.terminationHandler to call handleProcessTermination on unexpected exit
Implement private transitionState(to:) with validation preventing invalid transitions
Add OSLog logging for all state transitions and errors
Implement deinit calling stop() synchronously via DispatchSemaphore for cleanup
Add atexit handler registration to stop daemon on app termination
Write unit tests using mock Process for state machine validation
Write integration tests spawning real process for health check verification

CodexAppServerManager.stop() async - gracefully terminates app-server process
CodexAppServerManager.restart() async throws - stops then starts with backoff
CodexAppServerManager.healthCheck() async throws -> HealthStatus - polls /health endpoint
CodexAppServerManager.port: Int - port number app-server is running on

codex.appserver.stopped - emitted when app-server reaches stopped state

edge_cases: Codex binary not found in PATH - throw binaryNotFound error with helpful message
All ports in range already in use - throw portUnavailable error listing tried ports
App-server process exits immediately on spawn - detect via terminationHandler and report
Health endpoint returns non-200 status - retry with backoff then fail with healthCheckFailed
Health endpoint times out repeatedly - fail with startupTimeout after configured attempts
Process ignores SIGTERM - escalate to SIGKILL after grace period
start() called while already starting - return existing startup Task result
stop() called while already stopped - return immediately without error
restart() called rapidly multiple times - coalesce into single restart operation
App terminated via Cmd+Q - ensure daemon stopped via atexit handler
App force quit via Activity Monitor - daemon may orphan (documented limitation)
System sleep/wake cycle - health check may fail temporarily, use retry
Network interface change - localhost should remain stable
Codex CLI updates while running - existing process continues until restart
Port freed but immediately rebound - retry port detection
Process spawns but health never succeeds - timeout and cleanup process
failure_modes: FM-01: Binary not found - user notification with install instructions link
FM-02: Port conflict - retry with next port in range, then fail with list of tried ports
FM-03: Startup timeout - stop spawned process, transition to error state, log details
FM-04: Health check failure - retry 3 times with 500ms interval, then fail
FM-05: Unexpected termination - auto-restart up to maxRestartAttempts, then fail permanently
FM-06: SIGTERM ignored - SIGKILL after grace period, log warning about unclean shutdown
FM-07: Too many restart attempts - disable auto-restart, require manual intervention
FM-08: Process spawn permission denied - fail with sandbox permission error
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Engine/CodexAppServerManager.swift and Tests/CodexAppServerManagerTests.swift. Remove any imports or references from other files. No user data or configuration affected since manager is stateless code. If daemon was running, it will be orphaned until manual kill or system restart.

notes: This atom is critical for the Codex integration path. The lifecycle manager pattern mirrors how we handle Claude CLI processes but adds the complexity of a persistent daemon with health monitoring. Design decisions here affect X003-EVENTS (output parsing) and X004-SESSION (state persistence). Consider extracting a generic ProcessLifecycleManager protocol if patterns emerge.

risks: Process management is inherently complex with many failure modes and race conditions
Codex CLI app-server mode may have undocumented behaviors or change between versions
Port conflicts with other developer tools could cause frequent startup failures
Auto-restart logic could mask underlying issues and create confusing user experience
Orphaned daemon processes if Blaze app is force-quit bypassing cleanup handlers
mitigations: Comprehensive state machine with validated transitions prevents race condition bugs
Pin to specific Codex CLI version initially with version check on startup
Wide port range (100 ports) and clear error messages when all ports exhausted
Log all restart attempts prominently and disable after maxRestartAttempts with user notification
Document limitation of force-quit orphaning and provide manual cleanup instructions
risk_register.blast_radius: Medium - manager is used by adapter layer which is used by session layer. Bugs could prevent all Codex communication. However, failure is isolated to Codex path and does not affect Claude or Gemini adapters.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If manager proves unreliable, fall back to single-shot process spawning without persistent daemon. This loses session persistence but maintains basic functionality. Can also disable app-server mode entirely and use standard CLI invocation.

persistence: No persistence in this atom - manager state is ephemeral and resets on app launch. Session persistence handled by X004-SESSION which uses manager as dependency.
